subject: Observability add-ons pricing — usage vs committed slab for tracing + dashboards
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mendes <aisha.mendes@clearwave.health>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons pricing — usage vs committed slab for tracing + dashboards

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the time yesterday — good to hear where ClearWave wants to land on observability economics while you ramp the streaming ingestion. Attached is a concise starter packet (redwood_usage_pricing_v3.pdf) with two straightforward paths for the tracing + retention + dashboard bundle:

1) Usage-first (low-friction):
- Tracing ingest billed per 100K spans; storage billed per GB/month for retention.
- Dashboards included as part of the visualization add-on, metered by active dashboards/month.

2) Committed slab (predictable unit economics):
- Monthly committed credits that cover a slab of trace ingest, storage, and dashboard seats.
- Overage rates are lower and we offer a commit discount (tiered).

Key items I wanted to flag for you: retention beyond 12 months adds storage overhead (we modeled 13–18 months in the attached), and long-tail traces are the main driver of cost — we recommend a two-tier retention plan (hot 30d, warm 12–13m).

I've included a short dashboard mock (mvp_visual_dashboard_mock.png) to align on scope so pricing maps to the visual we discussed. If you can share the procurement contact and any required PO cadence, I can put together a SOW draft and a couple of side-by-side price examples (monthly commit for 12 months vs purely usage).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood_usage_pricing_v3.pdf, mvp_visual_dashboard_mock.png
From: Aisha Mendes <aisha.mendes@clearwave.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing — usage vs committed slab for tracing + dashboards

Jordan —

Thanks for the packet. A few quick clarifications so I can take this to procurement/legal: 

- We like the committed slab concept if it reduces variability. Are there standard discount bands for a 12-month commit vs 24-month?
- For tracing: can you confirm the per-100K-span price and whether sampling at ingest affects the billable span count?
- Retention: we need 13 months for audits with the option to archive to cold storage at lower cost after 6 months. Any SLA impacts?

Also, procurement will want a single SOW and a DocuSign link. Please cc our procurement lead: Tom Alvarez (tom.alvarez@clearwave.health).

—Aisha
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearWave Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mendes <aisha.mendes@clearwave.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing — usage vs committed slab for tracing + dashboards

Thanks Aisha — copied Marissa (Sales Manager) and Karthik (Solutions) to help finalize pricing and SOW. Quick answers below, plus I attached a draft SOW (clearwave_sow_draft.docx) that maps the slab to the dashboard scope.

Discount bands (illustrative):
- 12-month commit: 12% discount off list for the observability bundle
- 24-month commit: 20% discount off list
- Enterprise commit (>$500k ARR): please ask and we can carve extra concessions

Tracing billing / sampling:
- Billing is based on accepted spans ingested. If you apply client-side sampling before spans hit Redwood, that reduces billable spans. Server-side sampling that still sends all spans will count as ingested. We can also offer an SDK helper to implement aggressive client sampling for noise suppression.

Retention + cold archive:
- 13-month hot/warm retention is supported. We can configure automatic archive to cold storage after 6 months; cold storage is billed at a lower per-GB rate and is not included in the hot-slabs. SLA for archive retrieval is 24–48 hours by default; premium retrieval SLA available as an add-on.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to confirm the best discount we can extend for a 12-month commit with the dashboard bundle and a one-time onboarding credit.
2) We produce a redlined SOW and DocuSign envelope for procurement.

Marissa — can you propose a concession we can offer to close this one this month? Karthik — any technical caveats to call out for the SOW?

Best,
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mendes <aisha.mendes@clearwave.health>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing — usage vs committed slab for tracing + dashboards

Aisha / team —

Appreciate the urgency. We want to make the economics predictable for you while keeping the door open for scale. Here is what we can offer for a 12-month commit (ClearWave Health, DW-4829):

Commercial proposal (12-month committed slab):
- 15% off list across the tracing ingest and dashboard bundle for a 12-month commit (applies to committed credit consumption up to agreed slab).
- Additional 5% onboarding credit applied to month 1 invoice to offset migration effort (one-time).
- Cold-archive storage billable separately at a 40% discount to standard cold pricing when elected as part of the SOW.

If ClearWave signs a 24-month commit we can move to 22% off list (and increase onboarding credit to offset the longer term ramp).

Operational notes:
- We will include a clause in the SOW that documents the archive retrieval SLA (24 hours standard; 8 hours premium) and a runbook for sampling configuration so procurement/legal can see mitigations to cost drift.
- I will prepare a DocuSign envelope with the SOW and the pricing appendix today and share the link.

One ask: can Tom confirm whether ClearWave requires vendor-managed encryption/HSM keys for archived data? If yes, we'll add the integration scope to the SOW.

Jordan / Karthik / Evelyn — once Tom confirms encryption requirement, I'll finalize the DocuSign and pricing appendix.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks — the 15% + onboarding credit looks reasonable and likely acceptable to procurement. Confirming a couple of quick items before I route to legal:

- ClearWave will require customer-managed keys for archive data. Tom (cc'd) will follow up with specific KMS endpoints.
- Please mark the DocuSign SOW as: 12-month commit, slab: 1TB stored (hot/warm), 25M spans/month included, dashboards (10 active). Overage rates should follow the pricing appendix.
- Billing: prefer monthly invoicing with NET30.

If you can send the DocuSign link with the SOW updated for the KMS note, I'll get procurement/legal to review today. We aim to execute this week.

—Aisha

ClearWave Health
